title: test_channel.py:113: Test assertion incorrect for n_channels=1
description: test_minimum_channel_count asserts ch == 1 for synchronized_hop_channel(42, seed=0, n_channels=1), but the function actually returns 2. With n_channels=1, the implementation computes n = max(1-1, 2) = 2, so return 1 + (h % 2) yields either 1 or 2. For the specific inputs sfn=42, seed=0, the hash produces a value where (h % 2) == 1, so the function returns 2. This test would fail if executed. The test validates out-of-bounds behavior rather than catching the underlying implementation bug.
close_reason: Updated test assertion: n_channels=1 should expect 0 (only control channel), not 1. Implementation was already fixed to return 0 for edge case where no data channels exist.
